stem: Which of these is a renewable source of energy?

options.content: Solar power
Coal-fired power
Diesel
options.rationale: Diesel comes from oil, which is non-renewable.

options.content: Petrol

explanation: Renewable energy (solar, wind, hydro, biogas) is replaced naturally.

options.content: Producing in ways that do not use up or damage resources, so production can continue
Producing as much as possible in the shortest time, using whatever resources are available
options.rationale: This ignores the use of resources.

options.content: Producing only for the home market and never exporting
Producing goods by hand without any machines at all
options.rationale: Sustainability does not require hand production.

explanation: Sustainable production uses resources efficiently and protects the environment for the long term.

stem: A drinks company collects its empty glass bottles, washes them and fills them again. Which method of sustainable production is this?

options.content: Recycling
options.rationale: Recycling would melt the glass to make new items.

options.content: Using renewable energy
Reusing
options.rationale: Correct: the bottle is used again in its existing form.

options.content: Using biodegradable packaging

explanation: **Reusing** uses an item again; **recycling** processes it into new material.

stem: Which is an advantage to a business of becoming more sustainable?

options.content: No initial investment is ever needed
Prices of its products must always fall
It no longer has to follow any laws
Lower energy and waste costs in the long run

explanation: Using less energy, water and materials cuts costs over time and improves reputation.

stem: Which practice helps a farmer use land sustainably?

options.content: Keeping as many cattle as possible on one field
Clearing all trees from slopes
Planting the same crop every year without rest
Crop rotation and contour ridges
options.rationale: Correct: they protect soil fertility and prevent erosion.

explanation: Crop rotation, contour ridges and controlled stocking keep land productive.

stem: Why might a small business delay switching to recyclable packaging?

options.content: Customers never care about packaging
It may cost more per unit, raising costs or prices
Recyclable packaging is illegal for food and drink products
options.rationale: It is widely used for food.

options.content: Recycling increases the amount of waste

explanation: Sustainable options can have higher initial or unit costs, which small firms may struggle to afford.

stem: How can a community wildlife tourism project encourage local people to protect animals?

options.content: By allowing unlimited hunting by visitors
By sharing income from tourism with the community
options.rationale: Correct: people benefit from living animals.

options.content: By clearing the bush for crops
By keeping all income with outside investors
options.rationale: Local people would have no reason to protect wildlife.

explanation: When communities share the income, wildlife becomes a valuable resource worth protecting.

stem: Explain **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage for a manufacturer of switching to biodegradable packaging.

points.description: Advantage: better reputation / attracts environmentally aware customers or retailers.
Explained: higher sales / meets buyers' requirements / avoids future bans or fines.
Disadvantage: higher cost per unit / may not protect as well.
Explained: lower profit or higher price; customers may switch to cheaper rivals.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Biodegradable packaging improves the firm's image with customers and retailers who care about plastic waste, which can raise sales. However, it usually costs more per unit, so the firm must accept lower profit or raise prices, and some customers may switch to cheaper rivals.

explanation: Sustainable choices bring reputational benefits but may raise costs.

stem:
Thandeka manages a 40-room hotel in Victoria Falls. Most guests are foreign tourists. She is considering installing solar water heaters.

| Item | Amount |
| --- | ---: |
| Current monthly cost of gas for heating water | US\$620 |
| Expected reduction with solar water heaters | 70% |
| Cost of solar water heaters (installed) | US\$13,020 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the monthly saving from the solar water heaters.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate how many months it would take for the savings to cover the cost of the heaters.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Identify **two** other ways the hotel could produce its services more sustainably.

points.description: One way, e.g. rainwater harvesting / reusing towels / energy-saving lights.
Another way, e.g. recycling waste / buying local food / treating grey water.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Evaluate whether Thandeka should install the solar water heaters.

points.description: Uses data: saving US\$434 a month; cost recovered in 30 months.
Hot water available during power cuts / less dependence on gas supply.
Reputation with foreign tourists who value sustainability; marketing advantage.
High initial cost; finance needed; maintenance; cloudy days need back-up.
Compares with other uses of the money.
Justified conclusion.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The heaters would save US\$434 a month and pay for themselves in 30 months, after which the saving adds to profit for many years. They also reduce dependence on gas, and many foreign tourists prefer hotels that use renewable energy, which Thandeka can use in her marketing. The US\$13,020 cost is large and she may need a loan, and gas back-up is still needed on cloudy days. Because the cost is recovered in two and a half years and the reputational benefit is strong in tourism, Thandeka should install the heaters.

explanation: (a) US\$434. (b) 30 months. (c) Water, waste, lighting, local supplies. (d) Install, justified by savings and reputation.

stem: Farai's family farm near Masvingo grows maize and keeps cattle. Each year the topsoil on the sloping fields is washed away by heavy rain, and the family cuts trees from nearby hills for firewood. Yields are falling.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Identify **two** ways in which the farm is not using resources sustainably.

points.description: Soil erosion on slopes / poor land management.
Cutting trees without replanting / deforestation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain **two** methods the family could use to manage the land and forests sustainably.

points.description: Contour ridges / conservation farming / crop rotation.
Reduce erosion, keep soil fertile, raise yields.
Plant a woodlot / use efficient stoves.
Steady supply of firewood without destroying hills.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Discuss whether sustainable methods would benefit the farm as a business.

points.description: Higher yields over time from fertile soil.
Lower costs: firewood from own woodlot, less fertiliser.
Protects the farm's main resource for future years.
Costs: labour to build ridges, seedlings, years before trees mature.
Short-term loss of output or time; cash constraints.
Justified conclusion.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Contour ridges and crop rotation would stop topsoil washing away, so yields would recover and the farm would spend less on fertiliser. A woodlot would provide firewood without destroying the hills. These methods cost labour and money, and trees take years to grow, so benefits are not immediate. However, without them the farm's main resource, its soil, will keep declining. Sustainable methods would benefit the farm as a business in the long term, and the family should start with ridges, which are cheap and help this season.

explanation: Sustainable land and forest use protects the resources the business depends on.
hints: (a) Look at the soil and the trees.
(c) Compare short-term costs with long-term yields.
